question.problem: Find, in point-slope form, the equation of the line that passes through the points $(2,-5)$ and $(6,-3).$
question.worked_solution:
We know that the line passes through the point $(2,-5),$ so we can use $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,-5)$ in our point-slope formula. All that remains is to compute $m,$ and we can do this using the given points:

$$
\begin{aligned}m=\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}}=\frac{-3-(-5)}{6-2}=\frac{2}{4}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we substitute $m=\frac{1}{2}$ and the point $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(2,-5)$ into the point-slope formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-{y}_{1} & =m(x-{x}_{1}) \\ y-(-5) & =\frac{1}{2}(x-2) \\ y+5 & =\frac{1}{2}(x-2)\end{aligned}
$$
